title: CVE-2026-86413: Negotiate credentials sent to redirected origin
explain: The real code shows the flaw the report describes.

problems.evidence: 1 of 2 quoted lines appear nowhere in curl, e.g. 'if(Curl_auth_allowed_to_host(data) || conn->bits.netrc)'

summary: libcurl may send a Negotiate/Kerberos Authorization header to an unintended host after a redirect that contains userinfo in the Location header, bypassing cross-host authentication restrictions.

claims.text: The condition `data->state.creds || Curl_auth_allowed_to_host(data)` in `Curl_http_output_auth()` allows credentials set from a redirect URL to bypass the origin check.
claims.reasoning: The code at lib/http.c:874 shows exactly the condition described: if data->state.creds is set (non-NULL), output_auth_headers is called without requiring Curl_auth_allowed_to_host(data) to be true.

citations.note: Condition `if(data->state.creds || Curl_auth_allowed_to_host(data))` allows non-NULL creds to bypass origin check

claims.text: The origin check is performed only for credentials set via CURLOPT_USER options, not for credentials extracted from a URL's embedded userinfo.
claims.reasoning: The origin check functions are correctly implemented in vauth.c. The issue is that they are not called for URL-embedded credentials.

citations.note: Curl_auth_allowed_to_origin returns true only if allow_auth_to_other_hosts is set or origin equals initial_origin

claims.text: When a redirect's Location header contains `http://user:pass@evil.host/...`, `url_set_data_creds()` populates `data->state.creds` without invoking `Curl_auth_allowed_to_origin()`.
claims.reasoning: The URL credential extraction branch at lib/url.c:1456-1495 lacks any call to Curl_auth_allowed_to_origin, while the OPTION credential branch at lines 1428-1452 explicitly gates on it. A redirect URL with userinfo triggers the URL branch and sets data->state.creds without an origin check.

citations.note: OPTION credential branch (lines 1428-1452) checks Curl_auth_allowed_to_origin before creating creds
URL credential branch (lines 1456-1495) has NO origin check - only condition is !newcreds || !Curl_creds_has_user(newcreds)

claims.text: A valid SPNEGO/Kerberos token for the attacker‑controlled host is sent, even though the client never intended to authenticate to that host.
claims.reasoning: For SPNEGO/Negotiate, the token is generated from the client's ambient Kerberos TGT (via GSSAPI/SSPI), not from the URL's user:pass. The presence of any userinfo in the redirect URL sets data->state.creds, which bypasses the origin check in Curl_http_output_auth, causing the real Kerberos service ticket for the attacker's host to be sent.

citations.note: Curl_auth_create_spnego_message mints token from client's Kerberos TGT, not from URL credentials
Authorization: Negotiate header constructed with the minted token
Curl_output_negotiate called when Negotiate auth is picked and no Authorization header present

claims.text: A curl command that follows a redirect with userinfo in the Location header causes libcurl to emit an Authorization: Negotiate header to the redirected host.
claims.reasoning: The PoC demonstrates the exact code path: redirect with userinfo in Location -> url_set_data_creds sets data->state.creds via URL branch (no origin check) -> Curl_http_output_auth sees non-NULL creds -> calls output_auth_headers -> Negotiate path mints and sends real Kerberos ticket to attacker host. The control variant (no userinfo) sends no Authorization header.

citations.note: URL credential branch populates data->state.creds from redirect Location header userinfo
data->state.creds being non-NULL triggers auth header output including Negotiate

external_sources.title: http-auth
external_sources.for: Prior to commit 8f71d0fde51, the code required `Curl_auth_allowed_to_host(data)` for all credential sources, preventing this bypass.

key_reasons: The code at lib/url.c:1456-1495 extracts credentials from a redirect URL's userinfo without calling Curl_auth_allowed_to_origin, while the OPTION credential branch at lines 1428-1452 does check it.
The condition at lib/http.c:874 (data->state.creds || Curl_auth_allowed_to_host(data)) allows any non-NULL creds to bypass the cross-host auth guard.

For SPNEGO/Negotiate, the token is minted from the client's Kerberos TGT, not from the URL credentials, so even junk userinfo in the redirect is sufficient to trigger sending a valid service ticket for the attacker's host.
The PoC demonstrates the exploit works with a live Kerberos TGT, and the control variant (no userinfo) correctly sends no Authorization header.

This vulnerability exists in the current main branch (38703fe2) and was introduced by commit 8f71d0fde51 which removed the strict origin check while adding the asymmetric gating in url_set_data_creds.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and PoC. The vulnerability is confirmed: url_set_data_creds() extracts URL-embedded credentials on redirect without an origin check (lib/url.c:1456-1495), and Curl_http_output_auth() then bypasses the cross-host guard because data->state.creds is non-NULL (lib/http.c:874). For Negotiate, this causes a real Kerberos ticket for the attacker's host to be minted from the client's TGT and sent. We will fix this by gating the URL credential branch with Curl_auth_allowed_to_origin(), matching the OPTION branch.
